profile.summary: MVP (MultiView Projection) ranks candidate molecules for a tandem mass spectrum to annotate metabolites. It learns one embedding space for four views of the same compound: the molecular graph, the molecular fingerprint, a single spectrum and a consensus spectrum built from several spectra of that compound. A query spectrum or consensus spectrum is then compared with candidate molecules in that space.

summary_quotes.text: a novel framework for learning a joint embedding space between molecules and spectra by leveraging multiple data views: molecular graphs, molecular fingerprints, spectra, and consensus spectra.
MVP can be used to rank a set of molecular candidates given a spectrum.

sections.title: How it works
sections.body: MVP has one encoder per view and a contrastive loss over every pair of views. The molecule encoder is the same as JESTR's: a 3-layer graph convolutional network, a pooling layer and two fully connected layers. Spectra and consensus spectra are sets of peaks; by default each peak is represented by its chemical formula (FormSpec), encoded by a 3-layer MLP and then a transformer encoder with 2 attention heads. A binned-spectrum variant (BinnedSpec) is also provided. At inference any molecule view can be paired with any spectrum view; the authors report the graph to consensus spectrum view (mol-cs) as best.
sections.source_locator: Paper: Overview, Encoders, Comparative Study on Spectra Representation

quotes.text: MVP employs four encoders, one per view, and optimizes a contrastive loss across all pairwise view combinations
MVP uses the same graph encoder as JESTR - a graph convolution network (GCN) of 3 layers followed by a pooling layer and an MLP with 2 fully connected layers
Peaks are first encoded by a 3-layered MLP, and then the set of peaks is fed into a transformer encoder consisting of 2-attention heads
We denote the MVP spectra representation as FormSpec, whereas the binned version is referred to as BinnedSpec.
MVP with the mol-cs ranking view outperforms other tools across all metrics for both candidates by mass and formula.

sections.title: Versions and reproducibility
sections.body: Two pretrained checkpoints trained on MassSpecGym are distributed in the Hugging Face Space HassounLab/MVP: msgym_formSpec.ckpt and msgym_binnedSpec.ckpt. At the reviewed GitHub commit, the GitHub repository holds the code and params files but no checkpoint files, although the paper says pretrained models are available there. The GitHub repository and the Space carry no licence. A result should name the variant (FormSpec or BinnedSpec), the ranking view and whether consensus spectra were used.

strengths.text: Can annotate with consensus spectra that combine several measurements of a compound, which the authors report outperforms aggregating per-spectrum rankings.

quotes.text: we show that annotation using query consensus spectra significantly outperforms rank aggregation strategies based on constituent spectrum annotation.

quotes.text: Using the consensus spectrum view, MVP achieves 36.0 and 14.0% rank@1 when retrieving candidates by mass and formula, respectively.

run_guide.summary: Clone the MVP Hugging Face Space (which holds the code and both MassSpecGym checkpoints), install the requirements, download the preprocessed MassSpecGym files, and rank candidates with the pretrained FormSpec model.
prerequisites: A GPU is recommended by the authors for large data sets.
The preprocessed MassSpecGym archive from Zenodo record 15223987.
